behavior.arguments: rdi = struct base; rdx = [rdi+0x10] (a pointer whose first two qwords are read); rax = [rdi+0x20] (cursor). No other argument is read.

edges.at_first_bound: when cursor == [rdx], [rdi+0x20] becomes [rdx+8]; e.g. cursor 100, first bound 100, second bound 200 -> cursor 200.
edges.one_step_back: when cursor != [rdx], [rdi+0x20] becomes cursor - 8 (wrapping); e.g. cursor 108, first bound 100 -> cursor 100; cursor 0, first bound 100 -> 0xfffffffffffffff8.
edges.second_bound_not_compared: the wrap path never compares cursor against [rdx+8]; only [rdx] is compared.

behavior.entry_shape: Opens with endbr64; one conditional jump (je), zero calls; two rets, one per path.
behavior.return_rule: If [rdi+0x20] == [[rdi+0x10]] then [rdi+0x20] = [[rdi+0x10]+8], else [rdi+0x20] = [rdi+0x20] - 8 (wrapping modulo 2^64). No other field is written. rax holds the stored value incidentally; no return value of note is claimed.

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, without a guessed loader or Ghidra rebase. The ELF section table maps .text with file offset = VA - 0x1000; the retained .eh_frame has equal file offset and VA. The tools resolve sections rather than assuming one global VA/file-offset relationship.

incoming_pattern_scan.note: Byte-pattern scan over the full .text section (70,370,352 bytes) for e8 sites whose rel32 lands on the window start; zero sites found. This is explicitly not a complete xref census: indirect calls, tail jumps, and PLT references are out of scope for the scan.
incoming_pattern_scan.relocation_note: Exactly one R_X86_64_RELATIVE record in .rela.dyn names this window as addend (full-section scan: 80,022 .rela.dyn + 278 .rela.plt entries).
